correctness.rationale: For every detector event in the stated polarization-preserving beamsplitter model, the two \(\phi\) Bell states have equal likelihood because their relative sign joins orthogonal polarization sectors and cannot affect photon-count probabilities. Bayes/MAP success is therefore at most \(3/4\), and the standard 50:50 analyzer attains \(3/4\) by distinguishing both \(\psi\) states while leaving only the \(\phi\) pair unresolved. A wrong Bell-label correction is a nonidentity Pauli, whose Haar-average pure-state fidelity is \(1/3\), so the exact optimum is \(5/6\). The finite checker only replays exact rational arithmetic; the structural proof is analytic.
